page: The Microsoft Azure DC8eds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture and hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 8 dedicated Intel vCPUs paired with 32.0 GB of memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. For low-latency I/O operations, the instance includes 472 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and supports Azure Premium Storage options for external disk volumes.

Without onboard hardware accelerators or GPUs, compute tasks rely entirely on the dedicated Intel processor cores. The inclusion of a 472 GB NVMe SSD directly attached to the host provides cost-efficient local throughput for scratch spaces, indexing, and ephemeral data handling without requiring immediate reliance on external block devices. Tradeoffs include the lack of bundled public IPv4 networking and specialized vector extensions, focusing its capacity toward conventional enterprise execution.

This resource balance suits transactional relational databases, intermediate caching services, continuous integration runners, backend enterprise application hosting, and structured batch processing requiring fast scratch space.
description: The Microsoft Azure DC8eds_v6 is an x86_64 general-purpose server powered by dedicated Intel processor cores on Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 8 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 4.0 GB per core ratio. The configuration integrates 472 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage alongside support for Premium Storage tiers, delivering fast read and write access for applications with intensive temporary I/O demands. It operates without discrete GPUs, directing all computing capacity through the dedicated host processors. Because local NVMe storage is bundled, it provides cost efficiency for input-output intensive processes without external disk overhead. The server fits database engines, caching tiers, container hosts, and enterprise web serving workloads requiring balanced memory and compute resources.
